coauthors.name: Ali Etemad
coauthors.affiliation: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Queen's University, Canada
coauthors.relevance_evidence: PhD supervisor; 134 arXiv papers scanned (affective computing, multimodal/physiological ML, self-supervised learning, group fairness). Zero papers whose title or abstract mentions culture, cultural/moral values, cross-cultural comparison or value alignment. Fairness work ('Some Optimizers are More Equal') is demographic group fairness in vision models, no cultural or value dimension.

coauthors.name: Hatice Gunes
coauthors.affiliation: Department of Computer Science and Technology, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Leads LLM work on aligning agent behaviour with human norms and preferences: 'GRACE: Generating Socially Appropriate Robot Actions Leveraging LLMs and Human Explanations' (arXiv:2409.16879) - 'robots need to handle complex tasks while both adhering to social norms and accommodating individual preferences... integrating common-sense knowledge with human preferences, often conveyed through human explanations'. This is norm/value alignment of LLM-driven agents, plus related work on socially appropriate actions (StARS, 'Mind the Context') and 'Multimodal Gender Fairness in Depression Prediction: Insights on Data from the USA & China' (cross-national data comparison). Caveat: her work is HRI/affective computing rather than LLM cultural-values benchmarking; no paper of hers is explicitly about cross-cultural differences in LLMs.
